title: Ford Bronco Engines by Year
description: Every factory engine in the Ford Bronco by year: the 170 and 200 sixes and 289 and 302 V8s, the 300 six, 351 and 400 V8s, and the 2021+ EcoBoost engines.
intro: Ford built the Bronco from 1966 to 1996, first as a compact 4x4 and from 1978 on the F-series chassis, and brought the name back for 2021. The smaller Bronco II and today's Bronco Sport are separate models.
Pick a year to see every engine offered that model year, with its code, rated horsepower and the trims it came in. Each engine links to its full specs.
The early Bronco used the 170 and 200 sixes and the 289, then 302, V8. The 302 was the only engine from 1975.
The full-size Bronco arrived with the 351M and 400 V8s.
The 300 six and the 302 and 351 V8s, with fuel injection on the 302 from 1985 and a high-output 351.
All engines were fuel-injected: the 300 six, the 302 and the 351.
The last full-size Broncos used the 302 and 351 V8s; the six was dropped after 1992.
The new Bronco uses the 2.3 and 2.7 EcoBoost engines, with a 3.0 EcoBoost V6 in the Bronco Raptor from 2022. The ratings shown are on premium fuel.
